sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This temporary visa lets the aged parent of a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen stay temporarily in Australia.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- have an eligible child who is a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen
- be old enough to receive the age pension in Australia
- not have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (Subclass 870) visa when applying for this visa.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- live in Australia for up to 2 years
- work and study in Australia (you will not receive government support)
- apply for a permanent Contributory Aged Parent (subclass 864) visa.

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text:
From AUD35,430 over 2 instalments for a single applicant. Concessions apply in limited circumstances.

For more information on additional fees that may apply, go to the ‘About this visa’ page and click on Cost.

Cost concession

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See tab.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: The demand for Parent visas is greater than the number of places available each year. As a result, there are long processing times for these applications. For more information on processing times see Parent visa queue release dates.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- live in Australia for up to 2 years
- work and study in Australia (you will not receive government support)
- apply for a permanent Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864).

Apply for a Contributory Aged Parent (subclass 864) visa

You can apply for the permanent subclass 864 visa as a 2 stage process by first applying for a Contributory Aged Parent (Temporary) (subclass 884) visa. Applying for the subclass 884 visa before the subclass 864 visa allows you to spread the cost of the visas over several years.

You must apply for a permanent Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864) before your subclass 884 visa expires to ensure you meet all applicable lodgement criteria.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a temporary visa. You can stay in Australia for 2 years.

The visa period starts on the date we grant the visa.

The visa allows you multiple entry into Australia. You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want within 2 years.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You cannot stay in Australia longer by extending or reapplying for this visa. You can apply for a different visa.

You can Explore your visa options.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You can include members of your family in your application when you apply.

You must include details of all your family members in your application form, even if they are not migrating.

Family members who apply for the visa must meet our health and character requirements. Family members who are not coming to Australia might also need to meet our health and character requirements.

Learn more about health requirements.

Learn more about character requirements.

Newborn child

Find out what to do if you had a child.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
This visa costs from AUD35,430 for a single applicant. There are additional charges for each family member who applies with you. Concessions apply in limited circumstances.

Pay for this visa in 2 parts called instalments. You need to pay the first instalment when you apply and the second instalment when we ask you to.

You might also need to pay other costs for each applicant for health checks, police certificates and biometrics. For more information, see Fees and charges for other services.

To find out what your visa will cost, see current visa pricing. See more about visa fees and charges.

Cost concession for eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste visa applicants

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application.

We will charge eligible applicants the lower visa application cost during the application process. We will recognise eligible applicants when they apply with a valid passport from one of the specified countries.

Family members are also eligible for the lower visa cost. We base this on the passport of the primary applicant (or visa holder who satisfies the primary visa criteria).

The primary applicant must hold a valid passport issued by one of the following countries:

- Federated States of Micronesia
- Fiji
- Kiribati
- Nauru
- Palau
- Papua New Guinea
- Republic of the Marshall Islands
- Samoa
- Solomon Islands
- Timor-Leste
- Tonga
- Tuvalu
- Vanuatu

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text:
You, and any family members who apply with you, must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you apply and when we make a decision on your application.

If you apply for this visa in Australia while on a temporary visa with a no further stay condition, your application will be invalid. This is unless you apply for a waiver of this condition.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
The demand for Parent visas is greater than the number of places available each year. As a result, there are long processing times for these applications.

Applications for this visa are subject to capping and queueing. We process them in the order we receive them.

For more information on processing times, see Parent visa queue release dates.

Your application might take longer to process if:

- you do not complete it correctly
- you do not include all the documents we need, or if we need more information from you
- your information takes a long time to verify.

We can only process your application if you pay the correct visa application charge. We will notify you if you have not paid the correct amount and return your application, if necessary.

For more information on Migration Program outcomes against planning for each migration program year, read the Reports on Migration Programs.

Assessment

We assess applications for this visa in 2 stages:

- We will make an initial assessment to check eligibility to either add the application to the queue or refuse it.
- As places become available, we will release applications from the queue for final assessment.

Do not arrange to stay permanently in Australia until we grant your visa. We will let you know in writing if we grant you the visa.

Consider another visa

Other Parent visas available include the:

- Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864). This is a permanent visa. We may process Contributory Aged Parent visas faster, but they cost more.
- Contributory Aged Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 884) followed by a permanent Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864). This 2 stage visa process costs more than the Aged Parent visa (subclass 804). It also costs more than applying directly for the Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864), however, the cost is spread across the 2 visas over a longer period.
- Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870).

This is a temporary visa that allows parents to visit their children in Australia for up to 3 or 5 years at a time for a maximum total of 10 years.

You can view all visa options on our Visa list page.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You and your family members must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

See what conditions might apply to this visa on our visa conditions page.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of the following eligibility criteria to be eligible for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Not have this visa
sections.text: You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a sponsor
sections.text:
You must have an eligible sponsor.

Usually, an eligible child will sponsor you. If your child is under 18, an eligible relative or community organisation can sponsor you.

We must approve the sponsorship.

For more information on eligible sponsors, change the switch at the top right of the page to ‘Sponsors’.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the balance of family test
sections.text:
You must meet the balance of family test.

You meet the test if:

- at least half of your children and step-children are eligible children, or
- there are more eligible children living in Australia than any other single country

For more information and examples of how the test is applied, visit balance of family test.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be this age
sections.text: You must be old enough to receive the age pension in Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the health requirement
sections.text:
You, and any family members who apply for the visa with you, must meet our health requirement.

We might also ask that other non-migrating family members meet the requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the character requirement
sections.text:
You, and any family members who apply for the visa with you, must meet our character requirement.

We might also ask that other non-migrating family members meet the requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have paid back your debt to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you or any family members owe the Australian Government money, the debt must be paid back or there must be an approved arrangement to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Not have had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused
sections.text:
We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application. This means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused before.

In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused. For more information, see Limitations on applications in Australia.

If you are applying for a visa from outside Australia, see Can I go to Australia.

If you need immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Sign the Australian Values Statement
sections.text:
If you are 18 years of age or older, you must:

- have read, or had explained to you, the Life in Australia booklet
- sign an Australian Values Statement. This confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We will not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text: You must meet all of the eligibility criteria to be eligible for this visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Check your passport. If you need help with your application, get someone to act on your behalf.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Check your passport
sections.text: You and anyone who applies for the visa with you must have valid passports before we grant the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance, they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

To learn more, see authorised recipients.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > If you have an existing Parent visa application
sections.text:
If you have applied for a different Parent visa but we have not made a decision on it, you must withdraw that application when you apply for this visa.

To withdraw your other application, complete Part B of Form 47PA Application for a parent to migrate to Australia.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
Gather all your documents, including those for any partner or dependants who might be applying with you. You will also need your sponsor documents.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text:
There are consequences if you do not give us accurate or complete information.

To learn more, visit providing accurate information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
We need proof of your identity. If you cannot prove your identity:

- we will refuse your visa application
- we might not grant you another visa for 10 years
- we might not grant any family members you listed on your application a visa for 10 years.

Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name, if applicable.

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Sponsor documents
sections.text:
An eligible sponsor must sponsor your application.

Your sponsor must complete Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Balance of family documents
sections.text:
You must show us that you meet the balance of family test.

You can show this by giving us:

- evidence of how you are related to each child
- evidence of each child's Australian citizenship or country of permanent residence
- evidence that your child should not be included in the balance of family test (for example, their death certificate).

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text:
We might ask you for character documents, including police certificates. Do not arrange a police check until we ask you to.

Learn more about police certificates.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- give you immigration assistance, complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Send written notification or your forms with your paper application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants under 18 documents
sections.text:
For every dependant under 18 years old who is applying with you, provide:

- identity documents
- evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate
- character documents, if applicable.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants under 18 documents > Parental responsibility documents
sections.text:
You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who:

- has a legal right to decide where the child lives, and
- is not coming to Australia with the child.

They must complete either:

- Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years or
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to stay in Australia on this visa.

Alternatively, you can show us:

- an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or
- that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate.

You must include:

- an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, for example, a passport or driver’s licence
- adoption papers or other court documents, if applicable.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants over 18 documents
sections.text:
To be included in your visa application as a dependent child, your child must be:

- under 18 years of age
- over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner
- over 23 years of age, unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations, and dependent on you or your partner.

For every dependant 18 years of age or older who is applying with you, provide:

- identity documents
- evidence of your relationship with them, for example a birth or marriage certificate
- documents about their other relationships, if applicable
- character documents
- proof of dependency.

If your child is likely to turn 23 while we process your application, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you due to disability. For more information on visa processing times, see Parent visa queue release dates.

Proof of dependency

You need to prove that this person is dependent on you. You must provide:

- a completed Form 47A Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over
- proof of your relationship with the dependant, for example, a birth certificate or adoption papers.

You must also prove this person has been financially dependent on you for at least 12 months before you apply. You could provide:

- proof they live with you
- their tax records
- proof they are currently studying.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Partner documents
sections.text:
Provide us with:

- identity documents
- character documents
- evidence of your relationship with them, for example your current marriage certificate or documents that prove you have been in a de facto relationship for at least 12 months before you apply
- documents about other relationships, if applicable.

Documents that prove your de facto relationship include:

- joint bank account statements
- billing accounts in joint names
- joint leases or mortgages
- documents that show you have lived at the same address as your partner.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Photographs
sections.text:
Provide 4 recent photos of anyone included in the application.

Photographs must be:

- passport-size (45mm x 35mm)
- less than 6 months old
- good quality colour – we will not accept laser copies
- a view of your full face
- taken against a plain light-coloured background.

You can wear untinted prescription glasses. If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, you can show only your face.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

You must give us original certified copies and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not need to be accredited, but, on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating.

These details must be in English.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Certify
sections.text:
Do not certify police certificates. You must send us the original versions.

All other documents must be certified copies. This includes:

- non-English documents
- English translations.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Keep
sections.text: Keep a copy of your completed application, including all supporting documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Send
sections.text:
Send us:

- original police certificates
- certified copies of all other documents
- as much relevant information as possible to help us make a decision on your application
- each document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing
- all documents with your application, if possible.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
Online lodgement is not available for temporary Contributory Aged Parent visa applicants. You must apply for the visa on paper. You must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application.

You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply on paper
sections.text:
Complete Form 47PA Application for a parent to migrate to Australia.

Your sponsor must complete Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.

Each member of your family aged 18 years or over must also complete Form 47A Details of child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over. This applies even if they are not migrating.

You must complete all forms in English.

You must pay the first instalment when you apply. For payment options see how to pay.

You cannot apply for this visa in person. You must send your application by post or courier to the address on the form. Include all required documents, forms and evidence of payment of application charge with your application.

Do not send original documents (except for police certificates) with your application. You must only send certified copies.

You should keep a copy of your completed application for your own records, including any supporting documents.

If any of the above steps are incomplete, your application may be invalid. We do not process invalid applications. We will notify you if this is the case, and if requested, return your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application and documents. There may be other things you need to know and might need to do.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Importing your paper application
sections.text:
After you or someone else has submitted your paper application, you can import it into your ImmiAccount. You can do this after you receive your acknowledgement letter.

Importing your application into ImmiAccount gives you access to online services. This makes it easier to manage your application.

You can use our online services in ImmiAccount to:

- attach supporting documents to your application
- view messages we send to you
- update your details
- view the status of your application.

Follow these steps to import your application:

- Create a new ImmiAccount or log into your existing ImmiAccount. See instructions on how to use ImmiAccount.
- Once you log in, import your application by entering your:

- application ID
- date of birth
- identity document number (ImmiCard, passport or Titre de Voyage number).

For more information, see Apply and Manage your application in ImmiAccount.

You can import both new and on-hand applications.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
We cannot provide updates on your application's progress within normal processing times. We will let you know if you need to give us anything more.

Learn more about processing times at Parent visa queue release dates.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text:
You must tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. We need to know because you must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when we make our decision.

If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return.

Learn about visa expiry.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: We will let you know when you need to complete health examinations.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photos). We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Send more information
sections.text:
If you have imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use it to upload any additional documents that you did not send with your application.

Alternatively, you can send us additional documents using the Parent visa processing centre form.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Pay the second instalment
sections.text: You must pay a second instalment before we will grant the visa. We will send you an invoice when it is due. If you do not pay the invoice, we will refuse your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family members
sections.text:
You might be able to add family members to your application before we make a decision.

Complete and send us Form 1436 Adding an additional applicant after lodgement using ImmiAccount or the Parent visa processing centre form.

You will also need to give us evidence of your relationship and a copy of the family member’s passport.

Any family members you add to your application after you apply must be in Australia when you add them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family members > Newborn child
sections.text: Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Tell us as soon as you can if you make a mistake on your application.

To do this, complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers.

If you have imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use it to upload the completed form. Alternatively, you can send it to us using the Parent visa processing centre form.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Tell us if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- give you immigration assistance - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Send us your forms using ImmiAccount or the Parent visa processing centre form.

For more information, see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
You need to let us know about changes to your:

- phone number
- email
- address
- passport
- relationship status
- family composition, including the birth of a child

You should also tell us if you want to withdraw your application.

See what to do if your situation changes.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Stay lawful
sections.text:
Make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application.

When you apply for this visa in Australia, we are likely to grant you a bridging visa. If your current visa expires before we make a decision on your application, the bridging visa will start. You can stay in Australia on the bridging visa while we process your new visa application.

Do not cancel your current visa. If you do, you may:

- be staying in Australia unlawfully
- not be eligible for a bridging visa.

Learn more about visa expiry.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
You must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when we make a decision on your application.

We will let you know our decision in writing.

If we grant you the visa, we will let you know:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

You should keep a copy of our decision.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you:

- why we refused the visa
- if you have a right to a review of the decision

We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.

New step description

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you must do when you have this visa

You and your family members must meet all visa conditions and obey all Australian laws.

Tell us if things change

See what to do if your situation changes.

What you can do on your visa

See your visa expiry, conditions and work and study entitlements in VEVO.

See how long you can stay

This is a temporary visa. You can stay in Australia for 2 years.

To see when you must leave, use VEVO.

Travelling on your visa

You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid.

See your visa expiry and conditions in VEVO.

Proving you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

To get proof of your travel in and out of Australia, request your international movement records.

Working

This visa enables you to work in Australia. You will have Australian workplace law protections. You can read about your workplace rights and entitlements.

Staying longer

You cannot stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You must apply for a new visa if you want to stay longer. You can Explore visa options.

Permanent Pathway Processing Options

If you want to stay in Australia permanently, you must apply for a Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864) before your subclass 884 visa expires to ensure you meet all applicable lodgement criteria.

In exceptional circumstances we might allow you to apply for the subclass 864 visa after this. For more information see Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 864).

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

Ensure your visa is still valid

See what to do if your visa has expired or is about to expire.

At the border

Use the SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > After you leave
sections.text:
Proving you have been to Australia

To get proof of your travel in and out of Australia, request your international movement records.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > Things to note
sections.text:
- You must be a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen
- You must agree to support the applicant and their family for their first 2 years in Australia
- Apply to be a sponsor using Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > With this visa the applicant can
sections.text:
- live in Australia for up to 2 years
- work and study in Australia (visa holder will not receive government support)
- apply for a permanent Contributory Aged Parent (subclass 864) visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > Cost
sections.text:
There is no fee to sponsor an applicant. But you have financial responsibilities.

For more information, go to About this Visa tab and use the sponsor toggle at the top of the page. Then you can navigate to the Cost for the sponsor and ‘Sponsor obligations’ sections.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
The demand for Parent visas is greater than the number of places available each year. As a result, processing times for these applications are lengthy.

For an indication of processing times for this visa, see Parent visa queue release dates.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Scope of sponsorship
sections.text:
Your sponsorship covers the main visa applicant and any family members who apply for the visa with them.

You can sponsor more than one parent for this visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Cost for the sponsor
sections.text: There is no cost to sponsor a visa applicant. However, as a sponsor you will have financial obligations.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Sponsor obligations
sections.text:
For the first 2 years the visa holder is in Australia on this visa, you must agree to provide them and any family members who come with them with:

- support
- accommodation
- financial assistance.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Withdraw your sponsorship obligations
sections.text:
You can withdraw your sponsorship at any time before we decide on the visa application.

You must tell us in writing and include:

- your full name
- your date of birth
- the file reference number or Client ID from the application.

If you withdraw your sponsorship before we grant the visa, we may refuse it. We may ask the applicant to find another sponsor.

You cannot withdraw your sponsorship after we grant the visa. But, if you do not comply with your sponsorship obligations, we might cancel the visa.

Send your withdrawal request to us using the Parent visa processing centre form.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Be suitable to sponsor
sections.text:
To sponsor your parent for this visa, you or your cohabiting spouse or de facto partner must be:

- an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident, or an eligible New Zealand citizen, and
- settled in Australia, and
- 18 years of age or older

You must agree to provide support, housing and financial help for the first 2 years the applicant lives in Australia. You must also support any members of the applicant's family who apply with them.

You can sponsor more than one parent.

Alternative sponsorship arrangements

You can sponsor a visa applicant on behalf of a child under 18 if you are:

- an Australian citizen, an Australian permanent resident or an eligible New Zealand citizen
- settled in Australia
- 18 years of age or older.

You must be:

- the child’s cohabiting spouse
- the child's relative or guardian
- a relative or guardian of the child's cohabiting spouse.

Or a community organisation can sponsor an applicant where:

- there is a relationship between the organisation and the applicant's child
- a senior representative of the organisation agrees to sponsor the applicant
- the organisation is lawfully established in Australia
- the organisation has been actively operating in Australia for at least one year
- the organisation can meet its financial commitments.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Check that both you and the applicant are eligible.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
Provide accurate information.

You need to show us proof that you are:

- a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen
- related to the main applicant

We use the information in the application to make our decision. It will help the applicant if you give us as much information as possible.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents > Sponsor documents
sections.text:
You must prove your relationship to the applicant

Give us evidence that you are related to the applicant, for example:

- a birth certificate
- a marriage certificate
- a death certificate
- an adoption certificate
- family status certificates or family books if officially issued and maintained.

Prove you are a citizen or permanent resident

To prove that you are an eligible citizen or permanent resident, give us:

- your citizenship certificate
- your passport
- your valid visa (for eligible New Zealand citizens)
- evidence you are settled in Australia.

Prove you are an eligible community organisation

If your community organisation is sponsoring the applicant, give us:

- your certificate of registration
- proof your representative can act for the organisation, for example, authorisation from the board or management committee
- proof you can financially support the applicant after they arrive in Australia
- proof the organisation is lawfully established in Australia and has been actively operating in Australia for at least one year
- proof of your organisation's relationship with the applicant's child.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents > Translate
sections.text:
You must have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original copies and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not need to be accredited, but, on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating.

These details must be in English.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Apply
sections.text:
Complete Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.

Give the completed form and all other documents to the applicant to submit with their visa application.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let the applicant know when we have received their application and documents.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > Withdraw sponsorship
sections.text:
Tell us if you want to withdraw your sponsorship.

You can withdraw your sponsorship before we grant the visa. Send us your withdrawal request using the Parent visa processing centre form.

You cannot withdraw as a sponsor after we grant the visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
You need to tell us if you can no longer meet your obligations, or if any information has changed since the applicant submitted their information.

Tell us of any changes in your situation using the Parent visa processing centre form.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text: We cannot give updates on applications within the standard processing time. You should wait for us to contact you.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let the applicant know our decision in writing.

If we grant the visa, we will advise the applicant:

- the visa grant number
- the date their visa starts
- their visa conditions.

If we do not grant the visa, we will advise the applicant:

- why we refused the visa
- their review rights, if any
- the time limit for requesting a review of the decision, if applicable.

We will not refund the application fee if we refuse the application.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > How long your sponsorship obligations last
sections.text: Your sponsorship obligations last for 2 years.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Your obligations
sections.text: You must agree to provide accommodation and financial help to applicants you sponsor for their first 2 years in Australia. You need to make your commitment in writing.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Withdraw your sponsorship obligations
sections.text:
You can withdraw your sponsorship at any time before we decide on the visa application. You must inform us in writing and include:

- your full name
- your date of birth
- the file reference number.

Send your withdrawal request to us using the Parent visa processing centre form.

If you try to withdraw your sponsorship after we grant the visa, we may not release you from your sponsorship obligations.

If we do release you from your sponsorship obligations under the visa, we are likely to cancel the visa. We will then send you a letter releasing you from your sponsorship.
